title: Every public item has two stable paths, and missing_docs is not enforced
description:
hire-core/src/lib.rs:3-19 and hire-attestors/src/lib.rs:3-22 both declare every module `pub mod` and then flat-re-export its contents with `pub use`. That commits the crate to two permanent paths for each item — `hire_core::assurance::IdentityAssurance` and `hire_core::IdentityAssurance` — so the module layout can never be reorganised, and rustdoc lists everything twice. Callers in-tree already use both styles. Pick one: keep the flat re-exports and make the modules private (`mod assurance;`), or keep the modules public and drop the duplicate `pub use`.

Second, neither crate sets `#![warn(missing_docs)]` or `#![deny(missing_docs)]`, so undocumented public API is not caught. Current gaps, all reachable from the crate root: hire-core/src/trust_bundle.rs has no `//!` module header (the only module in the crate without one) and no docs on `TrustBundle.trust_domain` (:9) or `TrustBundleStore::new` (:41); hire-core/src/signer.rs:16 `SignerError` and all four of its variants (:17-24) are undocumented, as is `hire-attestors/src/lib.rs:90 AttestorError` and its variants; hire-grpc/src/service.rs:16 `WorkloadApiService`, its three public fields and `new` (:23) have no docs, and neither does hire-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs:86 `AttestError`. Every `pub fn new()` and `pub fn is_available()` on the eight attestors is undocumented except ssh.rs:31.

Filed as one hygiene issue rather than one per item; the fix is the lint plus a pass.
